subject: Economics
title: Impact of externalities on third parties

external_costs.label: External costs: costs of an economic transaction imposed on third parties not involved in it

external_benefits.label: External benefits: benefits of a transaction received by third parties not involved in it

stages.name: Impact of externalities on third parties
stages.title: Impact of externalities on third parties
stages.sub: After this, the student can explain why external costs and benefits matter for people outside the transaction.

steps.q: A factory and its customers agree a price for making and buying paint. The family living next door breathes in the fumes. Did that family take part in agreeing the deal?
steps.right: No, they had no say in it
steps.wrong: Yes, they helped set the price
steps.hint: Think about who actually sat down and agreed the sale.

steps.q: The factory pays its workers and suppliers, and the customer pays the factory. Does anyone pay the neighbours for the fumes they breathe in?
steps.wrong: Yes, the price already covers it
steps.hint: Money changes hands between the factory and the buyer. Does any of it reach the neighbours?

steps.q: The fumes drift from the factory's own land onto the neighbour's garden, without either side intending it. Does the effect stay contained inside the factory-customer deal, or does it move beyond it?
steps.right: It moves beyond the original deal
steps.wrong: It stays contained inside the deal
steps.hint: Fumes do not stop at the factory fence. Where do they end up?

steps.q: A café opens on a quiet street and passers-by enjoy the smell of fresh coffee for free, without buying anything. If a chemical plant instead makes nearby residents ill for free, in both cases who is actually affected by a deal they had no part in?
steps.right: People outside the original buyer and seller
steps.wrong: Only the buyer and seller themselves
steps.hint: The café owner and customer, or the plant and its customer, made the deal. Who else feels the result?
